subject: Social Science
chapter: 11. Grassroots Democracy — Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas
central_question: How do Panchayati Raj institutions enable rural people to participate in local decision-making, development and self-government?
in_scope_units: Rural needs and local decision-making — the example of Lakshmanpur
Panchayati Raj System — self-government and the village, block and district three-tier structure
Gram Panchayat and Gram Sabha — voters, direct participation, elections and the Sarpanch or Pradhan
Exemplary Sarpanchs — Dnyaneshwar Kamble, Vandana Bahadur Maida and Popatrao Baguji Pawar
Panchayat administration — Panchayat Secretary, Patwari, meetings, records and land maps
Child-Friendly Panchayat Initiative — Bal Sabhas, Bal Panchayats, Sikkim and Rajasthan examples
Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad — coordination, development plans, funds and schemes
Inclusion and representation — disadvantaged sections and reservation of one-third of seats for women
State variation and common objectives — active village management and development
Ancient administrative thinking — Kauṭilya's Arthaśhāstra and levels from villages to regional headquarters
banned_topics: Detailed functions of urban local bodies from Chapter 12
Complete structure of national government from Chapter 10
Modern party politics and election campaigning beyond the chapter

known_pitfalls.claim: The Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat are the same body.
known_pitfalls.correction: The Gram Sabha consists of enrolled adult voters, while the Gram Panchayat is the elected village-level institution.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Panchayati Raj system has only a village level.
known_pitfalls.correction: It has village, block and district levels.

known_pitfalls.claim: Children have no place in local democratic discussion.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter describes Bal Sabhas, Bal Panchayats and child-friendly initiatives.

recommended_example_progression: Connect local needs with self-government using the Lakshmanpur example.
Reconstruct the village, block and district tiers.
Compare inclusive leadership and development work using the Exemplary Sarpanchs section.
Practise discussion of local issues and solutions using a Bal Panchayat class activity.
Apply Panchayati Raj institutions to village problems.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Refer to the chapter-end 'Questions, activities and projects' Questions 1-4 on page 171.
